title: What amrit asks
hook: the five Ks, the daily banis and the four things avoided
carry: amrit's big yes lives in small daily keeps
tomorrow: prepare for months, or take it and grow? two Sikhs disagree.

segments.voice: Yesterday, a sign-up sheet, a pen on a string, and a head already on the palm: when ready. Simran didn't sign. She made a list instead.

The notes app on Simran's phone has a new page called what amrit asks. She expected the list to be dramatic: courage, devotion, giving your head. Then she copies out what the code actually says, and it's oddly small. A comb. A pair of cotton shorts. A steel bracelet. Prayers at dawn and at bedtime. A kind of meat not eaten. For the boldest picture in yesterday's lesson, why is the list so ordinary?
screen: `A NOTES PAGE: WHAT AMRIT ASKS.` → `A COMB. COTTON SHORTS. A BRACELET.` → `WHY SO ORDINARY?`

segments.voice: Here's the list, from the Rehat Maryada, the Sikh code of conduct, in three parts. First, the five Ks, kept on the body: kesh, uncut hair; the kanga, a small wooden comb; the kara, a steel bracelet; the kachhera, cotton undershorts; and the kirpan, a sword kept sheathed. Second, the daily banis, the Nitnem: set hymns at dawn, beginning with Japji, Rehras in the evening, and Sohila at night. Third, the four kurahits, the things avoided: cutting the hair; eating kutha, meat killed the ritual way; sexual relations outside marriage; and tobacco. Now the puzzle. Why is the head-on-your-palm step made of combs and morning prayers? Because a vow you feel once can fade. A vow you touch at the sink every morning is harder to lose. The big yes gets broken into small things you'll meet every single day. And here's the surprise in Simran's list, the thing to tell a friend tonight. A Sikh who has never taken amrit may already keep some of it. Simran's hair is uncut. She wears a kara. She reads Japji on most mornings. Her list isn't a wall between her and amrit. It's a map, and it shows how far she's already walked.
screen: `THE FIVE Ks, KEPT ON THE BODY.` · `THE NITNEM: DAWN, EVENING, NIGHT.` · `FOUR KURAHITS, AVOIDED.` · `A BIG YES IN SMALL DAILY THINGS.` · then, large: `WHAT IS ASKED.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers, slowly, the things you already keep, not only religious ones: a habit you've held for years, a promise you haven't broken, a way you treat your family. One finger each. Then rest your hands and notice how many are down.
What is asked. In the code: the five Ks, the daily banis, and four things avoided, all kept every day.
Keep this one: amrit's big yes lives in small daily keeps, the five Ks and the banis. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: At the amrit ceremony the five who give amrit explain the rehat aloud: the five Ks, the daily banis and the four things to avoid. Those who take amrit keep them every day.
